prompt:
I need the front end for Housewire. A home-automation builder for households, where a family's tinkerer composes routines by wiring together triggers, conditions and actions for the devices around the house, with an optional code view for each step.

Who's using it: Emeka Fairweather, a high-school chemistry teacher and hobbyist programmer who set up his family's smart-home devices. His partner and two kids use the routines but don't edit them.

What they're doing right now: Bedtimes have slipped since the switch from daylight saving time, so Emeka is building a 'School-Night Wind-Down' routine. On Sunday–Thursday at 8:15 p.m., if either kid is home according to their phone presence, the routine should dim the living-room lights to 30%, turn on the hall night-light, pause the kids' tablets' Wi-Fi at 8:45, and send a heads-up to both parents. It should skip on any day marked as a holiday in the family's shared school calendar. He's arranging the steps, adding a branch for when the 15-year-old has late swim practice, writing a short expression for the time window, and testing it against last Tuesday's events to see what would have fired.

What's in the system at this point: Household 'Fairweather Home' with 27 devices: 11 lights (with rooms and dimming support), 3 smart plugs, 1 thermostat, 2 door sensors, the router with 4 per-device Wi-Fi controls, and 4 phones used for presence (Emeka, Ruth, Ada 15, Tobi 11). 9 existing routines, such as 'Morning Lights' (enabled) and 'Away Mode' (disabled), each with trigger, steps and last-run time. Ada's swim practice is Tue/Thu until 8:30 p.m. The school-holiday calendar marks 6 dates through January. The event history covers the last 7 days of presence changes, door openings and light states for dry-run testing. The routine draft has 9 steps so far, one of them a condition written as `weekday in [Sun..Thu] and not holiday(today)`.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
